correctness.rationale: All fixed-dimension hypotheses and boundary cases are explicit. For d<m, common mean and variance plus independent-coordinate CLTs imply exchangeable iid Gaussian normalized limits and a positive rank gap of order sqrt(n). Splitting at N=n-floor(sqrt(n)) makes the prefix winning set stable, because a Chebyshev union bound gives suffix variation O_P(n^(1/4)) while the prefix cutoff gap is of order sqrt(n). Conditional on the prefix, Fourier frequencies of the selected suffix have modulus <=q_k^(d floor(sqrt(n))) with q_k<1 by nonresonance. The negligible probability of rank switching transfers this to the actual maximum; at frequency zero the rank is uniformly distributed. Fourier uniqueness gives joint independent uniform phase and rank. The exact inequality for each losing subset relative to the maximal subset is <=B^(-G_n), and G_n diverges in probability, yielding the total-face volume phase by Slutsky. For d=m, the single product has vanishing Fourier coefficients directly. The packaged exact checker verified 8063 finite subset comparisons from its actual path; it is expressly not an infinite-limit certificate.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 preprint poses exactly the general maximum-criterion conjecture for continuous independent but coordinate-heterogeneous cuts. Its Theorem 1.9 transfers Benfordness from maximum to frame but does not establish the desired maximum limit generally. The major 2025-2026 Fang--Miller follow-up, Theorem 5, already establishes all d under globally iid cuts with finite moments of all orders and bounded smooth density; Section 3.1 expressly leaves independent non-identical coordinates as future work. The present theorem covers independent coordinate-heterogeneous laws with only common finite second moments and nonresonance, including fully discrete examples excluded by the follow-up, and strengthens the marginal conclusion to uniform face-label asymptotically independent of leading-digit phase. Searches of primary papers and public mathematical records found no direct dominating theorem, subject to the stated residual literature risks.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may exist in more general random-walk mixing/conditional Fourier literature under terminology not identified by the searches.
The distinct label-independence conclusion is not necessarily novel as an abstract random-rank mixing lemma, though its application and low-moment theorem are not in the inspected papers.
The adjacent 2025 stick-fragmentation preprint was compared by abstract only, not enough to exclude every ancillary theorem; the principal close box-fragmentation follow-up was inspected in full.
The newer 2025/2026 theorem already settles the smooth iid all-dimensional subclass, which must not be claimed as new.

value.rationale: An explicitly proposed natural probability conjecture concerns the leading digits of maximal lower-dimensional faces of randomly shrinking boxes. The newer all-dimensional proof already handles a globally iid smooth subclass but not the physically natural heterogeneous coordinate cut laws. The present theorem supplies the fixed-dimensional complete common-moment class under minimal ordinary-CLT assumptions plus sharp arithmetic nonresonance, including concrete nonidentically distributed discrete cuts with no density at all. The joint uniform law of the maximizing coordinate subset and its digit phase is a natural structural invariant and yields the exact coupling of maximum/frame volume phases. This is motivated by the original geometric object rather than an artificial low-index slice; it does not claim new rates, dependent cuts, or an independent audit.
